1.title: Face cars together and switch off
1.say: Pull the two cars nose to nose with fronts close but not touching. Turn both keys off. Set both parking brakes.
placements: working car → nose to nose facing disabled car with fronts close but not touching and both engines off (in the video: black car facing red car in parking lot)
disabled car → nose to nose facing working car with fronts close but not touching and both engines off (in the video: red hood raised open over front engine bay with engine off)
watch_for: If the paint touches paint they are too close and can scratch.
If the cable ends cannot reach both batteries the cars are too far apart.
1.check_yourself: It should look like two fronts almost touching with both engines quiet and both hoods ready to open.
1.safety: Set the parking brakes so neither car can roll.

2.title: Open hoods and find batteries
2.say: Lift both front hoods. Prop both hoods open. Find the black box battery in each front corner.
placements: red car hood → raised open and propped over front engine bay (in the video: red hood held up on left side of frame)
black car hood → raised open and propped over front engine bay (in the video: black hood held up by wooden stick on right side of frame)
dead battery → black box with plus and minus posts in front corner of engine bay (in the video: left front corner of red car bay)
good battery → black box with plus and minus posts in front corner of engine bay (in the video: right front corner of black car bay)
watch_for: If you cannot see the black box you are looking in the wrong corner so check the other side.
If the hood will not stay up the prop is not seated so reset it before you lean in.
2.check_yourself: It should look like two open engine bays with a black box battery showing in each one.
2.safety: Hold the hood firm so it cannot fall on you.

3.title: Clip red clamps to plus posts
3.say: Clip the first red clamp to the plus post of the dead battery. Clip the second red clamp to the plus post of the good battery.
placements: first red clamp → plus post of dead battery usually marked plus or under red cover (in the video: front post on black box in red car on left side of frame)
second red clamp → plus post of good battery usually marked plus or under red cover (in the video: rear post on black battery in black car engine bay)
watch_for: If the red clamp wiggles the bite is loose so squeeze again until it holds.
If the red clamps touch each other or bare metal you have a short so keep them apart.
3.check_yourself: It should look like two red clamps biting both plus posts with metal teeth tight and cables hanging free.
3.safety: Keep the red clamps from touching each other or any bare metal.

4.title: Clip black to minus and metal
4.say: Clip the black clamp to the minus post of the good battery. Clip the other black clamp to bare shiny metal on the dead engine.
placements: black clamp from good side → minus post of good battery usually marked minus (in the video: side post on black battery in black car bay)
black clamp from dead side → bare shiny metal on dead engine away from battery (in the video: bolt on front frame above headlight with hand holding clamp)
watch_for: If the second black clamp is on the dead minus post it is wrong so move it to bare metal.
If any clamp touches moving parts it can catch so keep cables clear of belts.
4.check_yourself: It should look like one black clamp on the minus post and one black clamp on bare shiny metal away from the battery.
4.safety: Keep the second black clamp away from the dead battery and use bare metal only.

5.title: Start good car and wait
5.say: Sit in the good car. Turn the key to start. Let it run a few minutes to charge.
placements: key in good car ignition → turned to start with foot on brake until engine runs then released (in the video: hand turning key beside steering wheel with orange dash lights lit)
watch_for: If the good engine stops right away the key was not held long enough so start again.
If the dead battery gets no time it will not charge so wait a few minutes.
5.check_yourself: It should look like the good car running with dash lights on while the cables stay still.
5.safety: Keep hands and clothes clear of the spinning belts and fan.

6.title: Start dead car and unclip cables
6.say: Turn the key in the dead car to start it. Pull off the red and black clamps. Let the dead car run a few minutes alone.
placements: both black clamps → lifted off minus post and bare metal and held clear of engine (in the video: hand lifting clamp from battery area)
both red clamps → lifted off plus posts and held clear so no clamp touches metal (in the video: engine bays with clamps removed and cables clear of batteries)
watch_for: If the dead car dies right away the charge was too short so hook up and wait longer.
If a loose clamp touches metal while running it can spark so hold each one clear.
6.check_yourself: It should look like both engine bays with no clamps on and no cables near the spinning parts.
6.safety: Keep hands and clothes clear of the spinning belts while it runs.
